eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a modest high of 20°C or below at 37.5% for São Paulo on May 15, reflecting the approach of a new frente fria—a cold front blending a polar air mass with an oceanic system—that INMET and Climatempo forecasts indicate will arrive Friday, capping daytime highs around 19–21°C amid 65–86% rain chances and increased cloudiness. This marks a sharp cooldown from midweek peaks near 25°C on May 13–14, continuing May 2026's colder-than-average trend, including record lows earlier in the week. Ensemble model guidance from GFS and ECMWF supports suppressed temperatures via southerly winds advecting cool, moist air, though exact peak hinges on front timing and morning clearing; updated hourly INMET bulletins today could refine odds further before resolution based on official Mirante de Santana observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket evenly distributes implied probabilities across 17–21°C for Helsinki's highest temperature on May 16, mirroring the narrow spread in short-range weather model ensembles amid inherent forecast uncertainty two days out. The Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI) projects a daytime high near 15–16°C under partly cloudy skies with light southerly winds and low precipitation risk, while ECMWF and other global models show potential upside to 18–20°C if ridging builds and cloud breaks allow greater solar heating. Recent observations confirm cool conditions, with May 14 highs around 10–12°C following passing showers, but climatological mid-May averages of 16°C and moderating Baltic Sea influences add variability. New FMI and ECMWF updates on May 15 could refine the peak, as boundary layer mixing and urban effects in Helsinki further differentiate outcomes.
